newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma authorities restrict Suu Kyi movements - aide.
newsitem.headline: Burma authorities restrict Suu Kyi movements - aide.

text.p: Burma's military authorities have restricted opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi's movements and she has been told she cannot leave her house, an aide told Reuters by telephone on Wednesday.

"It is virtual house arrest. We were informed yesterday that she cannot leave her compound..." he said, adding that no reasons were given for the action nor was she told how long the restriction would remain in force.
The restrictions imposed on Suu Kyi by the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) followed student protests in the heart of the capital Rangoon before sunrise on Tuesday.

Police detained about 300 Yangon Institute of Technology students protesting against police handling of a brawl between some of their colleagues and restaurant owners in October. Most of the students were later released, a SLORC spokesman said.
Burmese authorities have barred access to Suu Kyi's University Avenue residence since Tuesday. Suu Kyi was not available for comment.

In a separate statement, the human rights group Amnesty International said five members of Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy's (NLD) youth wing had been detained by the military after they had left her house compound on Tuesday. "The compound is now sealed and no one can enter or leave," Amnesty said.
